clue.text: Idiot not entirely without feeling, shame one has quit

indicators.note: something not entirely present loses a bit, so the word for numbness drops its final letter

parts.note: to be without feeling is to be numb

indicators.note: one that has quit has left, so the numeral letter goes from the word for shame

parts.note: a shame, as in 'what a pity'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone insulting a fool who has become a little more sensitive, now that shame has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims NUMB to NUM; 'has quit' removes I from PITY, leaving PTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish and northern British slang word for a foolish, inept person; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Feature is familiar with broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken over the air, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase's synonym

parts.note: a person familiar with something knows it

explanation.surface: A news feature that the presenter already knows well goes on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that KNOWS is heard, giving a word spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial features include the eyes, mouth and the organ of smell in the middle of the face.

clue.text: Great musicians playing sitar with me

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: Top performers making music on the sitar alongside the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges SITAR plus ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural of a word for a distinguished conductor or virtuoso performer.

clue.text: Better money for big guns

parts.note: to better someone is to top them
brass is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A suggestion that more cash would buy bigger artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS is northern British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the most senior officers or bosses in an organisation are its big guns.

clue.text: Having rubbed out old boy, drug lord understood to be a slimy crawler

indicators.note: rubbing out erases, so the letters for old boy come out of the drug lord's name

parts.note: Pablo Escobar, the Colombian cocaine baron
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to have got something is to have understood it

explanation.surface: A gangland tale: a drug baron, having had an old boy killed, is seen as a slimy creep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbed out' looks like murder in the surface; here it removes OB from ESCOBAR, leaving ESCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary word for a snail, a creature that crawls along on slime.

clue.text: One of 12 with bow, as guitarist after a fiddle

indicators.note: after a fiddle the letters have been tampered with, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician with a bow, i.e. a violinist, joining a guitarist after taking up the fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fiddle' is the anagram signal, though fiddle and bow tempt a violin reading. The bow in the definition is an archer's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archer is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, depicted drawing a bow.

clue.text: A bit of music to be shared equally

parts.note: a piece is a single composition

explanation.surface: A snippet of music meant to be divided fairly among the players.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb meaning each, as when sums are divided evenly per person.

clue.text: Sticky stuff on bottom of cone in tree, more nutty

parts.note: goo is sticky gunk

indicators.note: one piece put inside another

parts.note: the fir is a conifer

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sticky resin oozing from the base of a cone up a conifer, a nuttier scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom of' takes E from 'cone', which 'in' puts inside FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a slang word for silly or eccentric, as is nutty in the sense of daft.

clue.text: Journeyman composer beginning to languish in winter, without success

indicators.note: the composer and initial go inside what remains
the word for success is taken away from the season

parts.note: a win is a success
Maurice Ravel, French composer of Boléro

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A jobbing composer who starts to wilt in the cold season after failing to make it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the success from the season, leaving TER; 'beginning to' gives L; 'in' places the composer and L within. 'winter' looks like the season but must be split.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman in the literal sense is someone who makes journeys, a voyager.

clue.text: Screened by fifth columnist, general dropping off

indicators.note: something screened by another is hidden behind or within it

parts.note: a fifth columnist is a traitor working within, a spy
Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A general, shielded by a secret agent, starts nodding off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screened by' signals insertion. Robert E. Lee is the crossword's favourite general; 'dropping off' means falling asleep, not falling away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dozing, nodding off to sleep, is drowsy.

clue.text: General places reflected in Indian city

indicators.note: the reflected word goes inside the city

parts.note: Agra, home of the Taj Mahal

indicators.note: a reflection shows a word backwards

parts.note: loci, the Latin plural for places

explanation.surface: A military man's postings mirrored in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' gives ICOL; 'in' signals insertion. 'General' is the definition here, though 9-across's general was Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman commander who governed Britain and conquered much of it in the first century.

clue.text: Knot tied, coveter set to be someone walking sneakily down the aisle?

definitions.text: someone walking sneakily down the aisle?

indicators.note: to knot is to tangle, so these words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A wedding image: a knot tied, a jealous suitor poised as someone creeping down the aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knot' rearranges TIED, COVETER and SET. The aisle is a supermarket's, not a church's.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-clothes security guard patrols a shop's aisles watching for shoplifters.

clue.text: Contrarily, was evil mind a French horn player?

indicators.note: taken contrarily, the word runs the opposite way

parts.note: to have done wrong is to have sinned
the mind, the brain

explanation.surface: An odd question about whether a wicked intellect belonged to a French horn player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrarily' turns SINNED into DENNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated British virtuoso of the French horn, who died in 1957.

clue.text: Question clothes a nudist designed for religious festival

indicators.note: clothing wraps around, so the question word goes round the rest

parts.note: why is a question word

indicators.note: something designed is laid out anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a naturist would get dressed for a church holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' gives ITSUNDA; 'clothes' is a verb, wrapping the question word round it, though it reads as garments for the nudist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter, has this traditional English name.

clue.text: Wine not half dry, where bottles kept a joke

indicators.note: not half means only one half survives, so the word loses its second two letters

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine
a wine rack stores bottles

explanation.surface: A wine connoisseur's quip about a fairly dry bottle stored in the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps WI of WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart, flippant remark, a quip or gag.

clue.text: Test of reading and learning, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A school exam covering reading and learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the first letters of 'of reading and learning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, as in a language exam conducted by speaking.

clue.text: Figure below zero turned around for everyone in economic region

indicators.note: in a down clue, the figure sits below the rest
turned around here means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal viewing, suitable for everyone
one is a number

explanation.surface: A figure below zero, a reversal of fortune for everyone in an economic bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned around' rearranges letters rather than reversing them, giving EUROZ; 'below' places the figure underneath in this down clue. U is the British film certificate for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of European Union countries using the single currency.

clue.text: Indian, post-Haydn, sounding game?

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and heard as one spelt differently

parts.note: Haydn sounds like 'hide and', so in the game hide-and-seek the word after it is seek

explanation.surface: An Indian person after a Haydn concert, asking about a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is hide-and-seek: Haydn sounds like 'hide-and', so what comes after is SEEK, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the faith founded in the Punjab, India, by Guru Nanak.

clue.text: President as fiddler

explanation.surface: A head of state described as a cheat or a violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of both the assassinated US president and a famous British violinist.

clue.text: In leak, one stopping vehicle to obstruct legislation

indicators.note: what follows is put in the word for leak

parts.note: news filters out when it leaks
I is the Roman numeral one, standing first as if stopping the vehicle
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A political leak: someone halts a bus to block a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals insertion into the word for leak; a leak filters out, as news does.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk at great length in a legislature so as to delay or block a vote.

clue.text: Flipping brilliant hiding data sheets in the kitchen

indicators.note: the reversed word hides the data inside it
flipping turns the word over, end to end

parts.note: lit means brightly illuminated
info, short for information

explanation.surface: A flipping clever way of concealing information sheets in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' gives TIL and 'hiding' takes the data inside. 'Flipping' also reads as a mild British expletive, disguising the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin rolls of metal foil used for cooking and wrapping food come off as sheets.

clue.text: God stands above bird, accepting son as the Creator

indicators.note: in a down clue, the god sits above the bird
in a down clue a word that stands is reversed upward

parts.note: Ra, the Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: accepting takes another piece inside

parts.note: the tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A god stands over a bird, taking a son in, as the creator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands' reverses upward in a down clue, giving AR; 'accepting' signals insertion. 'the Creator' suggests God, who is already in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter or sculptor creates works, so a maker of art is a creator.

clue.text: Fiddles embracing lively sonatas, or encapsulating the ultimate in dumb instruments?

indicators.note: the word for fiddles wraps around the rest

parts.note: fiddles and cons are both swindles

indicators.note: the rearranged letters enclose the final letter
lively means animated, so the letters are rearranged
the ultimate is the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Violins enclosing lively sonatas, perhaps hinting at silent instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lively' is the anagram signal; 'the ultimate in dumb' gives B, which 'encapsulating' places within; 'embracing' wraps the swindles round all. Fiddles are cons, not violins.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the deepest woodwind instruments of the orchestra, so they are instruments indeed.

clue.text: A shade cooler around start of winter

indicators.note: the cooler goes around the initial

parts.note: a fan cools the air

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A colder tone of colour as winter begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives W from 'winter', which FAN goes 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light yellowish-brown colour, named for a young deer.

clue.text: Written about in almanac, I remain like 17, perhaps

indicators.note: written about here means written backwards, turned round
the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: A writer featured in an almanac stays like the president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds NACIREMA in 'almanac, I remain'; 'Written about' reverses it. 17 is Kennedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Kennedy was a US president, so he was a citizen of the United States, as the example shows.

clue.text: Master on something stringed, as cellist

indicators.note: in an across clue, master placed on the end of the toy

parts.note: a yo-yo is a toy on a string
MA is a master's degree, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A virtuoso on a stringed instrument, described as a cellist.
explanation.walkthrough: The stringed thing is a toy, not an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The renowned American virtuoso of the cello, born in Paris in 1955.

clue.text: Critical supporter adds quality to piano parts

indicators.note: the first piece adds the next after it

parts.note: a piano's keys are its playable parts
a sound's tone is its quality

explanation.surface: A pianist's playing improves when the keys are given more tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adds' joins the pieces in order. 'Critical' means crucial here, not fault-finding.
explanation.definitionFit: The central wedge-shaped stone at an arch's crown that holds the structure together.

clue.text: Capital inspiring lieder is, for starters, the capital for a composer!

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the capital takes the initials inside

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland

indicators.note: for starters means the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A city full of art song is the ideal capital for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' gives LI; 'inspiring' means breathing in, so the Swiss capital takes them inside. The definition doubles up: a German capital and Irving Berlin, the songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: The German capital shares its name with Irving Berlin, the American songwriter.
